SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 6700
Date 6-6-35

FLYING DUTCHMAN
CREW FREED

Fine of Y. 200 Imposed by
Formosa Authorities

Giran, Formosa, May 11.
After undergoing the strictest ques-
tioning for several days, the crew of
three of the Shanghai ketch Flying
Dutchman, who ran foul of the Ja-
panese authorities on May 2, obtained
their freedom to-day—but only after
payment of a fine of Y.200.
Immediately after his release, Mr.
W. S. Gates, American member of the
crew, left for Taihoku to report to
the American Consul there.
In the meantime, his colleagues,
H. G. Wrede, 26-year-old German, and
Gene Roubin, a Russian, are prepar-
ing to leave the island at the first
opportunity.—Reuter.

Otto Kriez Fined Y. 200
Taihoku, May 11.
Otto Kriez, a Shanghailander and
the owner of the yacht Osten, who
was arrested in the middle of April
on a charge of entering the strategic
zone in Formosa without leave, was
brought up at the Taichu district
court to-day. After a short hearing,
he was fined Y. 200 for violating the
Shipping Law and released.
The Osten, with a crew of two,
Kriez and a Frenchman named
Severin Ruffio, sailed from Shanghai
on April 1 in an attempt to reach the
United States.—Reuter.

“飞翔的荷兰人”号
船员获释

台湾当局处以200日元罚款

台湾基隆，5月11日电。
上海双桅纵帆船“飞翔的荷兰人”号（Flying Dutchman）的三名船员于5月2日触犯日本当局，经过数日最严厉的讯问后，今日获得自由——但前提是缴纳200日元罚款。
美国籍船员 W. S. Gates 先生获释后立即前往台北，向当地美国领事馆报到。
与此同时，他的同事，26岁的德国人 H. G. Wrede 和俄罗斯人 Gene Roubin，正准备在第一时间离开该岛。——路透社。

Otto Kriez 被罚款200日元
台北，5月11日电。
上海居民、游艇“奥斯滕”号（Osten）船主 Otto Kriez 于4月中旬因涉嫌未经许可进入台湾战略区而被捕，今日在台中地方法院受审。经简短听证，他因违反《航运法》被罚款200日元并获释。
“奥斯滕”号载有两名船员，即 Kriez 和一名名为 Severin Ruffio 的法国人，于4月1日从上海启航，试图抵达美国。——路透社。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, MAY 5, 1935

Shanghai German Still
Held As Alleged Spy

Ruffio, 2nd Member Of Wotan
Crew, Said Released

TOKYO, May 4.—(Reuters).—It is learned here today that the small sailing-boat Osten, which left Shanghai for the United States on April 1, was detained at Taiko, Formosa, in the middle of that month.

The crew, consisting of Otto Kriez, a German, and Severin Ruffio, a Frenchman, were arrested on a charge of espionage, and taken to Tainan, in Taichu Prefecture, for an examination.

Ruffio has since been released, but Kriez is still in prison.

The authorities here declare that they have no information on the subject, but they are now conducting an investigation.

Ruffio 此后已获释，但 Kriez 仍在狱中。

此处当局声明他们对此事没有信息，但目前正在进行调查。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MAY 4, 1935
10507
S. B. EA
Another Boat, Two More Men Held In Formosa
No. D 6 700
Date 5/ 8/25

Simultaneous with the arrest on Monday of three Shanghailanders comprising the crew of the ketch "Flying Dutchman" by Formosan authorities at Taito, Mr. Otto Kriez (left), German, and Mr. Severin Ruffio (center), and their boat "Wotan III" (right inset) were seized by Formosa authorities on the same day at Talan on another alleged spy charge. Kriez and Ruffio left Shanghai on about April 1, continuing a round-the-world pleasure tour, and were bound for Manila and the South Seas.

2 Germans From Shanghai Also
Held, Boat Seized In Formosa

Members Of Separate Expedition From That Of
'Flying Dutchman' Arrested; Fate Of Members
Of Both Groups In Doubt As News Scarce

Simultaneous with the arrest of the three Shanghailanders comprising the crew of the "Flying Dutchman" at Taito, South Formosan militarized port, on Monday for alleged spying, Formosan authorities on the same day arrested two more Shanghailanders comprising a separate expedition and seized their boat "Wotan III" at Talan, west coast, on the same charge. THE CHINA PRESS learned from reliable sources last night that the two men were on a world tour. After remodeling their boat, they left early in April for America via Manila and the South Seas.

Alleged To Be Photographing
Mr. W. S. Gates, American, Mr. H. G. Wrede, 26, German, and Mr. Gene Roghin, 31, nationality either American or Russian, left Shanghai April 1 in their 53-foot ketch "Flying Dutchman" on a round-the-world cruise, ostensibly to search for gold in sunken ships. On May 1 they were seized at Taito on the charge of alleged spying, including illegal photographing of the coast.

The seizure of the "Wotan III" is the third spy scare in Formosa in the past few weeks.

The Takao branch of the Tainan High Court last Saturday ordered confiscation of the Netherlands tanker Juno and the imposition of a ¥2,000 fine on her master upon conviction of having violated Article III of the Japanese Marine Act by entering without permission into a fortified zone in the Pescadores. The master had claimed that he had sought refuge from a typhoon.

另一艘船及另外两人在台湾被扣
编号 D 6 700
日期 1925年5月8日

周一，台湾当局在台东逮捕了由三名上海外侨组成的双桅纵帆船“飞翔的荷兰人”号（Flying Dutchman）船员的同时，德国人 Otto Kriez 先生（左图）和 Severin Ruffio 先生（中图）及其船只“沃坦三世”号（Wotan III，右插图）也于同日在台湾塔兰（Talan）因另一项涉嫌间谍的指控被台湾当局扣押。Kriez 和 Ruffio 于4月1日左右离开上海，继续其环球休闲旅行，目的地为马尼拉和南洋。

另有两名来自上海的德国人
被扣，船只在台湾被没收

成员属于不同于“飞翔的荷兰人”号的独立探险队；由于消息匮乏，两组人员的命运均悬而未决

周一，在南台湾军事化港口台东，由三名上海外侨组成的“飞翔的荷兰人”号船员因涉嫌间谍活动被捕；与此同时，台湾当局以同样的罪名逮捕了另外两名组成独立探险队的上海外侨，并在西海岸的塔兰（Talan）扣押了他们的船只“沃坦三世”号。《字林西报》昨晚从可靠消息源获悉，这两人正在进行环球旅行。在改造船只后，他们于4月初出发，经马尼拉和南洋前往美洲。

涉嫌拍摄照片
美国人 W. S. Gates 先生、26岁的德国人 H. G. Wrede 先生以及31岁、国籍为美国或俄罗斯的 Gene Roghin 先生，于4月1日乘坐53英尺长的双桅纵帆船“飞翔的荷兰人”号离开上海，进行环球巡航，表面上是为了搜寻沉船中的黄金。5月1日，他们在台东因涉嫌间谍活动（包括非法拍摄海岸线）而被扣押。

“沃坦三世”号被扣是过去几周内台湾发生的第三起间谍恐慌事件。

台南高等法院高雄分院上周六下令没收荷兰油轮“朱诺”号（Juno），并对其船长定罪，因其违反《日本海事法》第三条，未经许可进入澎湖要塞区，处以2,000日元罚款。该船长曾声称他是为了躲避台风而寻求避难。

REPORT
Date May 2, 1935.

Subject Request from the Japanese Consul-General for information
regarding the yacht "Wotan" and its crew.
Made by D.S. Sansom Forwarded by M.B. Queirolo. O.O.

The attached translation of a telegram received by the
Japanese Consul-General from the Formosan Police refers to
two adventurers named Otto Diez, 24, German, and Severin
Ruffio, French-Eurasian, 25, who sailed from Shanghai on
April 6, 1934, aboard the yacht "Wotan 11," for America via
Manila.
Diez, in company with another German, Richard Knecht,
on May 12, 1932, sailed from Mannheim, Germany, aboard the
yacht "Wotan I," on a round-the-world adventure. Some two
years later they reached Moulmien, Burma, where they were
compelled to cancel the project on account of illness.
From Moulmien, they proceeded to Shanghai by steamer, arriving
here in May, 1934. In Shanghai they published a book
entitled "Adventures in a small boat." Five hundred of
these books were sold at $2.00 per copy, thus enabling them
to raise sufficient funds with which to purchase the "Wotan 11"
with the intention of resuming their travels. Knecht,
however, became indisposed, and his place was taken by
Ruffio. Knecht (referred to in the telegram as Creft)
resides at 240 Nanzing Road and is employed with Kunst
Albers, 110 Szechuen Road. He is about to remit funds to
Manila on behalf of these two men.
Whilst in Shanghai, Diez resided at 240 Nanzing Road.
He lived quietly and did not come to the notice of the police.
Ruffio was born locally. Nothing detrimental to his
character is known to either the Shanghai Municipal Police
or the French Police.
A copy of the book "Adventures in a small Boat" is
submitted herewith for favour of passing to the Japanese

Diez 曾与另一名德国人 Richard Knecht 于1932年5月12日在德国曼海姆乘坐游艇“沃坦I”号（Wotan I）出发，进行环球冒险。约两年后，他们到达缅甸毛淡棉，因病被迫取消计划。

在上海期间，Diez 居住在南京路240号。他生活安静，未引起警方注意。
Ruffio 在当地出生。上海公共租界工部局警务处或法国巡捕房均未掌握任何对其品行不利的信息。

page_data.en:
Translation

At 4 p.m. April 26, a small yacht called at Taian,
Taichu, Formosa. The crew of the vessel consisted of two
persons, one of whom was a German writer and artist named
Otto Zies (?), 24, residing at No.240 Nansei Dori (?),
Shanghai, and the other, a Frenchman named S.E. Ruffio,
unemployed, residing at Chateau d'Eau (?),the Bund, Shanghai.

As a result of interrogating of these two persons, the
following imformation has been obtained :-

The yacht left Shanghai on April 6 en route to Manila.
During the voyage the sails and the hull of the vessel were
damaged so they called at this port to make necessary repairs.
They proposed to make a trip to the U.S.A. via Philippine
Islands with the object of writing essays on travel and taking
photographs for illustration. The vessel "Wotan" (?) is an old
ship purchased at Shanghai and registered with the German
Consulate there. A relative of Otto Zies, named Creft (?), 30,
is at present operating a cigarette factory at the address given
as Otto Zies's residence. A sum of gold $200 has been remitted
to the Manila Post Office by Creft.

Investigations are being conducted regarding the two
persons in view of the suspicious nature of the articles in
their possession and of their movements.

You are, therefore, requested to verify the following
information and to communicate the results to us by cable
immediately :-

Have they resided in Shanghai ?
What is the object of their voyage ?
What are their connections with Creft ?
Other useful information.
page_data.zh:
译文

4月26日下午4时，一艘名为“沃坦”号的小型游艇停靠台湾台中泰安。该船船员由两人组成，其中一人是名为 Otto Zies (?) 的24岁德国作家兼艺术家，居住在上海南京路（Nansei Dori ?）240号；另一人是名为 S.E. Ruffio 的法国人，无业，居住在上海外滩 Château d'Eau (?)。

通过对这两人的讯问，获得以下信息：

该游艇于4月6日离开上海，前往马尼拉。航行途中，船帆和船体受损，因此停靠本港进行必要维修。他们计划经菲律宾群岛前往美国，目的是撰写游记文章并拍摄插图照片。“沃坦”号（?）是一艘在上海购买的旧船，并在当地德国领事馆注册。Otto Zies 的一位名为 Creft (?) 的30岁亲属，目前在 Otto Zies 住址所示地址经营一家卷烟厂。Creft 已向马尼拉邮局汇去200金元。

鉴于这两人随身携带物品的性质可疑及其行踪，正在对二人进行调查。

因此，请核实以下信息，并立即通过电报将结果告知我方：

他们是否居住在上海？
他们航行的目的是什么？
他们与 Creft 有何关系？
其他有用信息。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, MAY 2, 1935

FOREIGNERS HELD
AT FORMOSA

Espionage Charges Against
Americans

Tokyo, May 1.
Three Americans, one reported to be a retired naval lieutenant, are being held by the authorities at Taito, Formosa, charged with espionage, according to dispatches received from there to-day. In addition, at the little port of Taian, Formosa, one German and one Frenchman, allegedly from Shanghai, are also being held upon the same grounds.
The arrest of the Americans—whose names have not been made public by the Formosan authorities—came about after the small yacht in which they had been sailing was damaged so severely as to force them to put into shore.
Police immediately arrested them for landing without a permit, claiming that craft had evidently been damaged purposely in order to give the men an excuse for coming ashore. Furthermore, the police claim that they had been taking pictures of the coast-line. The Americans, however, claimed that they were merely on a pleasure sail from Keelung and were blown ashore. Their protests were unheeded, they being taken to court where they will be examined and forced to defend themselves against the charges of espionage which have been preferred against them.

"Hotbase" and "Kwass"
Meanwhile, a coincidence took place in the form of a second small yacht being blown ashore at Taian. The occupants of this vessel were a German and a Frenchman. Their note books indicated that they were from Shanghai and that they had intended to examine the coast-line. A faulty translation of their names as received from Formosa sounds something like "Hotbase" and "Kwass." They also are suspected of espionage.
According to information given out at the American Embassy, the officials there have not been informed of the plight of the Americans but an immediate investigation is to be made by members of the Embassy staff.—United Press.
page_data.zh:
16489
《字林西报》，1935年5月2日，星期四

外籍人士
在台湾被扣

针对美国人的
间谍指控

东京，5月1日。
据今日收到的发自当地的电讯称，三名美国人（其中一人据称为退役海军中尉）在台湾台东被当局扣押，指控犯有间谍罪。此外，在台湾小港口泰安，一名德国人和一名法国人（据称来自上海）也因同样理由被扣押。
对这些美国人（其姓名尚未由台湾当局公布）的逮捕，发生在他们乘坐的小型游艇严重受损迫使其靠岸之后。
警方立即以未经许可登陆为由逮捕了他们，声称该船显然是故意损坏，以便为这些人上岸提供借口。此外，警方声称他们一直在拍摄海岸线。然而，这些美国人声称他们只是从基隆进行休闲航行，被风吹上岸。他们的抗议未被理会，他们被带上法庭，在那里他们将接受审讯，并被迫对被提出的间谍指控进行辩护。

“Hotbase”和“Kwass”
与此同时，巧合的是，第二艘小型游艇也被吹到泰安岸边。这艘船的 occupants 是一名德国人和一名法国人。他们的笔记本显示他们来自上海，并打算考察海岸线。从台湾收到的他们姓名的错误译音听起来像是“Hotbase”和“Kwass”。他们也被怀疑从事间谍活动。
根据美国大使馆提供的信息，使馆官员尚未获悉这些美国人的困境，但使馆工作人员将立即进行调查。——合众社。
